## Table of Contents

### Classes

#### Public Classes

* [`openvas`](#openvas): Greenbone Community Edition (OpenVAS) as a docker compose stack, with what
it scans built from PuppetDB.

A bare include installs Docker, brings up the stack, sets an admin password,
and creates one target and one task per OS family. Nothing is scanned until
you start a task or set `scan_schedule_enabled`.

* [`openvas::target`](#openvas--target): Makes a node ready for credentialed scans from the openvas scanner.

#### Private Classes

* `openvas::config`: The compose file. Versioned here so the stack only changes through a module release.
* `openvas::install`: Docker, the compose plugin, and the install directory.
* `openvas::scans`: Puppet owns what Greenbone scans: one target and one task per OS family,
built from PuppetDB, plus the credentials they log in with and the admin
password it all runs as.

The desired state is rendered to a root-only JSON file and converged by
reconcile.gmp.py, a gvm-script run inside the gvm-tools container through
/usr/local/sbin/greenbone-reconcile. The exec only fires when the script's
check mode finds gvmd out of step, so a node joining or leaving PuppetDB
reaches the scan scope within one agent run on this host. Nothing changes
while a scan is running; the next run picks it up.

Targets use "Consider Alive": discovery by ping drops every node whose
firewall drops ICMP, and scanning an explicit list from PuppetDB doesn't
need discovery at all.

Run `greenbone-reconcile plan` on the host to see what apply would do,
including while a scan is running.

* `openvas::service`: Brings the stack up and keeps it up, current, and within its disk.

## Classes

### <a name="openvas"></a>`openvas`

Greenbone Community Edition (OpenVAS) as a docker compose stack, with what
it scans built from PuppetDB.

A bare include installs Docker, brings up the stack, sets an admin password,
and creates one target and one task per OS family. Nothing is scanned until
you start a task or set `scan_schedule_enabled`.

#### Examples

##### Install, with scans started by hand

```puppet
include openvas
```

##### Scan weekly

```puppet
class { 'openvas':
  scan_schedule_enabled => true,
}
```

##### <a name="-openvas--install_dir"></a>`install_dir`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\/[\w.\/-]+\z/]`

Directory holding compose.yaml and the reconciler's files. Letters, digits,
dots, dashes, underscores, and slashes only, as it ends up in shell commands.

Default value: `'/opt/greenbone-community-container'`

##### <a name="-openvas--feed_release"></a>`feed_release`

Data type: `String[1]`

Vulnerability feed release tracked by the data containers.

Default value: `'24.10'`

##### <a name="-openvas--feed_update_schedule"></a>`feed_update_schedule`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A[^\r\n]+\z/]`

When the feed images are pulled and the data containers refreshed, as a
systemd `OnCalendar` expression in the node's timezone. A run is skipped
while a scan is going, and a missed run isn't caught up at boot, so choose a
time the node is up and not scanning.

Default value: `'*-*-* 05:53:00'`

##### <a name="-openvas--web_bind_address"></a>`web_bind_address`

Data type: `Stdlib::IP::Address::V4::Nosubnet`

IPv4 host address the web UI binds to, on ports 443 and 9392.

Default value: `'127.0.0.1'`

##### <a name="-openvas--manage_docker"></a>`manage_docker`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether this module installs Docker through the `docker` class.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-openvas--admin_password"></a>`admin_password`

Data type: `Optional[Sensitive[String[1]]]`

Password for the `admin` user. When unset, one is generated on the node and
kept in `gvm-admin.conf` in `install_dir`, root only. It can't start or end
with whitespace, which gvm-tools strips when it reads the file.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_ssh_private_key"></a>`scan_ssh_private_key`

Data type: `Optional[Sensitive[String[1]]]`

Private key for credentialed scans of Linux hosts. Unset means those hosts
are scanned without logging in, which finds much less.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_windows_password"></a>`scan_windows_password`

Data type: `Optional[Sensitive[String[1]]]`

Password for credentialed scans of Windows hosts. Unset means those hosts
are scanned without logging in, which finds much less.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_login"></a>`scan_login`

Data type: `String[1]`

Account the scan credentials log in as, on every scanned node.

Default value: `'openvas'`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_purge"></a>`scan_purge`

Data type: `Boolean`

Remove every object in gvmd this module did not create, reports included.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_schedule_enabled"></a>`scan_schedule_enabled`

Data type: `Boolean`

Scan each OS family weekly. When false, targets and tasks exist but nothing
starts on its own.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_exclude"></a>`scan_exclude`

Data type: `Array[String[1]]`

Certnames to leave out of the scan scope.

Default value: `[]`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_schedule_starts"></a>`scan_schedule_starts`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], String[1]]`

First run per OS family (UTC, iCalendar DTSTART), repeated weekly on that
day and time. Defaults (in the module's data) are Saturday 16:00 UTC for
RedHat, 18:00 for Debian, and 20:00 for windows. Hiera merges into them, so
setting one family leaves the others where they are.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_default_start"></a>`scan_default_start`

Data type: `String[1]`

First run for any OS family not in `scan_schedule_starts`. With the default
hash that's none of RedHat, Debian, or windows, so this alone moves nothing.

Default value: `'20260912T220000Z'`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_max_hosts"></a>`scan_max_hosts`

Data type: `Integer[1]`

Hosts scanned concurrently per task.

Default value: `20`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_max_checks"></a>`scan_max_checks`

Data type: `Integer[1]`

Tests run concurrently per host.

Default value: `4`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_observer_user"></a>`scan_observer_user`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

Optional read-only gvmd user, for anything that pulls reports. It is created
with the Observer role and can see the managed tasks and their reports only.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvas--scan_observer_password"></a>`scan_observer_password`

Data type: `Optional[Sensitive[String[1]]]`

That user's password. Set both or neither: one without the other fails the
catalogue.

Default value: `undef`

### <a name="openvas--target"></a>`openvas::target`

Include this on the nodes you scan; the scanner itself takes `openvas`. It
creates the account the scanner logs in as. On Linux that is an account with
the scan key's public half, and on Windows a local administrator with the
scan password. It reads the scanner's own Hiera keys for the login and the
Windows password, so those are set once for both.

Safe to include everywhere before the Hiera values exist: without them it
warns and changes nothing, and starts working once they are set.

To use an account that already exists, set `manage_user` to false. On Linux
the class then only adds the key, and on Windows it does nothing.

#### Examples

##### In a profile every scanned node gets

```puppet
include openvas::target
```

##### Hiera, common to the scanner and the nodes

```puppet
openvas::target::ssh_public_key: "ssh-rsa AAAAB3Nza... openvas-scan"
openvas::scan_windows_password: ENC[PKCS7,...]
```

#### Parameters

The following parameters are available in the `openvas::target` class:

* [`ssh_public_key`](#-openvas--target--ssh_public_key)
* [`login`](#-openvas--target--login)
* [`manage_user`](#-openvas--target--manage_user)
* [`windows_password`](#-openvas--target--windows_password)
* [`ssh_key_name`](#-openvas--target--ssh_key_name)

##### <a name="-openvas--target--ssh_public_key"></a>`ssh_public_key`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A(ssh|ecdsa|sk)-\S+ \S+/]]`

The whole line from the `.pub` file, such as `ssh-rsa AAAA... openvas-scan`.
Needed on Linux.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvas--target--login"></a>`login`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The account name. Defaults to `openvas::scan_login`, then `openvas`.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvas--target--manage_user"></a>`manage_user`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to create the account. Set false for an account that already
exists or is managed elsewhere.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-openvas--target--windows_password"></a>`windows_password`

Data type: `Optional[Sensitive[String[1]]]`

The account's password. Defaults to `openvas::scan_windows_password`.
Needed on Windows when `manage_user` is true.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvas--target--ssh_key_name"></a>`ssh_key_name`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

The name of the authorised key, `<login>-scan` by default. Declared with
stdlib's `ensure_resource`, so another module describing the same key under
the same name, such as a second scanner sharing this account, declares it
once. The same name for a different key fails the catalogue.

Default value: `undef`

## Functions

### <a name="openvas--puppetdb_rows"></a>`openvas::puppetdb_rows`

Type: Ruby 4.x API

Runs a PuppetDB query, and answers with an empty list when PuppetDB is down or
the function isn't there at all. A scanner host should still converge the rest
of its catalogue when PuppetDB can't answer.

#### `openvas::puppetdb_rows(String[1] $query)`

Runs a PuppetDB query, and answers with an empty list when PuppetDB is down or
the function isn't there at all. A scanner host should still converge the rest
of its catalogue when PuppetDB can't answer.

Returns: `Any` The rows, or an empty list.

##### `query`

Data type: `String[1]`

The PQL query.
